videos.title: How the Tide Works
videos.plays: After the 0-2 intro, before play starts; replayable from the level's “How it works” button
videos.synopsis: A slowed-down explainer of 0-2's idea and tools. A path is a map f : I → X; a homotopy is a continuous movie of paths, one map F on the square I × I whose rows are the frames fₜ; rel A means the posts never move (the square's side edges). The Tide Glass scrubs t; the Spool makes homotopies by hand and hooks the ribbon onto stakes. What breaks a homotopy: a cut, a jump between frames, crossing water. A 3D demo on the flats plays beside a 2D diagram of the interval and the square.

scenes.title: A path is a map
scenes.description: Top-down over a ribbon between two posts. A bead slides along the ribbon while, in the diagram, a bead slides along the interval [0, 1]: s ↦ f(s).

scenes.title: A homotopy is a movie
scenes.description: The tide bends the ribbon from t = 0 to t = 1; five frames freeze as ghosts. The diagram becomes the square I × I, each frozen frame a row, the current frame a gold row at height t.

scenes.title: The Tide Glass
scenes.description: The movie scrubs back and forth; the diagram shows the Tide Glass slider and Z / X keys, and faint ghosts hug the ribbon on either side.

scenes.title: Rel A
scenes.description: The two posts pulse gold; the square's left and right edges light up: F(0, t) = a, F(1, t) = b for every t — the ribbon's ends are pinned (A).

scenes.title: The Spool
scenes.description: Gyroid walks to the ribbon, clicks to grab it, walks it out to a stake and clicks to let go; it hooks on. The diagram lights each control as it's used.

scenes.title: What breaks a homotopy
scenes.description: Three forbidden moves: a cut (the ribbon in two pieces, violet sparks), a jump (two neighbouring frames far apart), and crossing water at the pool shrine (the wet stretch violet).

scenes.title: Summary
scenes.description: Crane up over the flats; the diagram shows the summary card. Title card at 65.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Let’s slow everything down. This gold ribbon is a path: a map $f$ from the interval $I = [0, 1]$ into the flats.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Slide $s$ from 0 to 1, and $f(s)$ runs along the ribbon from one post to the other.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Now let the tide move it. At each time $t$ there’s a new path, $fₜ$. Here are a few frames.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Stack every frame and you get one map $F(s, t)$ on the square $I × I$: $s$ along the ribbon, $t$ through time. Each row of the square is one frame.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: So a homotopy is the whole movie — not just the first and last picture.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: The Tide Glass scrubs that movie. Press 3 to hold it; Z and X — or the wheel — move $t$ back and forth.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Watch the faint ghosts either side: in a real homotopy, neighbouring frames are always close together.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: And the posts? The ribbon’s ends never move, in any frame: $F(0, t) = a$ and $F(1, t) = b$ for every $t$.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: That’s a homotopy relative to $A$ — $rel A$ — where $A$ is the set of points on the ribbon that are pinned in place.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Your Spool makes homotopies by hand. Press 2, walk up to the ribbon and click to grab it.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Walk, and the ribbon follows. Every step is a new frame, so the movie stays continuous.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Click beside a stake to let go: the ribbon hooks on, and that point joins $A$ — one more point that stays put.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Three things break a homotopy. A cut: the ribbon has to stay in one piece.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A jump: no frame can leap away from the one before.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: And crossing water: every frame has to stay on the flats.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: So: a homotopy is a continuous movie of paths, and $rel A$ means the pinned points stay put. That’s all the shrines ask.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Bend, don’t break. Got it.

videos.title: Same Shape
videos.plays: After the 0-3 intro, before play starts; replayable from the level's “How it works” button
videos.synopsis: Homotopy equivalence, slowly: explicit maps f (eight → theta) and g (theta → eight, collapsing the bar), drawn as gold threads; a point's round trip lands near home and slides back (g∘f ≃ 1). Then the quick proof the level uses — one reef that deformation retracts onto both — contractibility, and the controls.

scenes.title: Same shape?
scenes.description: A figure-eight and a theta side by side in gold. The diagram asks X ≟ Y.

scenes.title: Maps both ways
scenes.description: Gold threads draw f from the eight to the theta, then g back. The diagram shows X ⇄ Y with f and g.

scenes.title: Round trips slide home
scenes.description: A bead travels p → f(p) → g(f(p)) and slides back to p along the eight. The diagram: g∘f ≃ 1, f∘g ≃ 1.

scenes.title: One reef, two spines
scenes.description: A two-hole reef slides onto a figure-eight, grows back, and slides onto a theta. The diagram: Z deformation retracts onto X and onto Y, so X ≃ Y.

scenes.title: Contractible
scenes.description: A solid reef slides onto a point; a loop around a ring's hole catches.

scenes.title: How to play
scenes.description: Controls for spines and Slide; Mirror spawn and their reflections.

scenes.title: Summary
scenes.description: Summary card; title card at 66.5.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Two reefs: a figure-eight and a theta. They look different. Are they the same shape?

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: In topology, “same shape” means something precise — maps both ways that can be undone, up to sliding.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Start with a map f from the eight to the theta: each loop of the eight goes once around one loop of the theta.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: The crossing goes to the middle of the bar. Each gold thread joins a point to where f sends it.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: And a map g back: squash the theta’s bar to the crossing, and wrap each side around a loop of the eight.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Now follow one point there and back: across to the theta by f, then home by g.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: It doesn’t land exactly where it started…

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: No — but it slides home along the eight. g after f is homotopic to the identity.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: When both round trips slide home, f is a homotopy equivalence: X and Y are the same shape.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: There’s a quicker way to prove it: find one reef that slides onto both.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: This reef deforms onto the eight… and onto the theta. Same shape.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A reef that slides onto a single point is contractible: the same shape as a point.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A loop around a hole catches. Proving the ring isn’t contractible has to wait for World 1.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: To prove a reef: Spool (2), click to start the thread, walk it through the beacons, click to stop — then Slide.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: And Mirror spawn come in pairs. Lash the solid one; the flickering one is only a reflection.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Same shape, different look. Let’s open that gate.

videos.title: Built from Cells
videos.plays: After the 0-4 intro, before play starts; replayable from the level's “How it works” button
videos.synopsis: Cell complexes, slowly: skeletons X⁰ ⊂ X¹ ⊂ X²; the sphere as a point and a disk; the torus as a square glued along a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹ (folded live); the projective plane along a a (crossing itself in 3D); χ; then Gyroid works a furnace to show the controls.

scenes.title: Built in stages
scenes.description: A point appears; two loops grow out of it and back (edges glued at both ends); a disk fills one loop. The diagram lists X⁰ ⊂ X¹ ⊂ X².

scenes.title: The sphere
scenes.description: A flat disk curls up as its whole rim is drawn to one point: a sphere. Diagram: e⁰ ∪ e² = S².

scenes.title: The torus
scenes.description: A square with arrowed edges a, b rolls into a tube (a meets a), then bends into a ring (b meets b). Diagram: a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹.

scenes.title: Arrows matter
scenes.description: A disk whose rim runs round loop a twice, the same way: it folds into a surface that passes through itself — the projective plane.

scenes.title: χ
scenes.description: Counting cells: points − edges + disks for each build.

scenes.title: At the furnace
scenes.description: Gyroid steps onto a furnace, clicks to forge the point, walks the track out and back to forge edge a, walks it again to write a, and clicks to press a disk along a (a hemisphere folds above the press).

scenes.title: Summary
scenes.description: The torus again; the summary card.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Everything in the Foundry is built in stages. First, points — the 0-cells.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Then edges, glued on by their two ends. Glue both ends to the same point and the edge becomes a loop.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Then disks, glued along loops. Each stage sits inside the next.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: The simplest sphere: one point, and one disk whose entire rim is crushed onto that point.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Like pulling the drawstring on a bag until the opening's gone.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: The torus: one point, two loops $a$ and $b$, and one square disk. Its rim is glued along $a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹$.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Watch matching arrows meet: the two a-sides glue into a tube, then the two b-sides bend the tube round into a ring.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Now one loop, $a$, and a disk whose rim goes round $a$ twice — the same way both times.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: There’s no room in our space to do that without the disk passing through itself. That’s the projective plane.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: And a count: points minus edges plus disks. That’s χ, the Euler characteristic.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Build the same place two different ways and χ comes out the same — though proving that waits for World 2.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Here's how it works at a furnace. Watch Gyroid.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Click the furnace with the Cell-Smith: that's the point.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Walk out along the track, round its loop and back onto the furnace: an edge, $a$ — a loop at the point.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Walk it again, the way its arrows point. That writes $a$ on the disk's rim — see “walked” on the panel.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Then click the furnace: the press glues a disk along $a$. A bowl — a hemisphere.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: And lash the Unglues — if one tears an edge, walk that track again.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Points, edges, disks. Let's build.

videos.title: New Spaces from Old
videos.plays: After the 0-5 intro, before play starts; replayable from the level's “How it works” button
videos.synopsis: Operations on spaces, slowly: the cone (a ring's hole fills and every loop slides to the tip); the suspension (two points → a circle → a sphere); the wedge (two rings touch at one point); the product (a small ring swept round a big one: a torus, with a cell for each pair of cells); the quotient (a disk's rim collapsed: a sphere); then the works' controls.

scenes.title: The cone
scenes.description: A glowing ring; its tip rises and pulls it into a cone. A loop on the rim slides up the cone and vanishes at the tip. Diagram: CX, X's cells plus one on each plus the tip; χ = 1.

scenes.title: The suspension
scenes.description: Two points sprout arcs to a tip above and below: a circle. The circle grows a double cone that rounds into a sphere. Diagram: S(S⁰) = S¹, S(S¹) = S².

scenes.title: The wedge
scenes.description: Two rings glide together until they touch at one point: a figure-eight. Diagram: X ∨ Y, cells add, minus one point.

scenes.title: The product
scenes.description: A small ring travels round a big one, sweeping out a torus. Diagram: the four pairs of cells, 1 + 2 + 1.

scenes.title: The quotient
scenes.description: A disk's rim is drawn to one point and it closes into a sphere. Diagram: D²/∂D² = S²; collapsing something contractible keeps the shape.

scenes.title: How to play
scenes.description: The works' controls: pick up, feed, choose the operation, take the result off the shelf, pull plugs.

scenes.title: Summary
scenes.description: Cone, suspension, wedge, product, quotient — and the cells each adds.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A cone: take a space and join every one of its points to a single new tip.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Cone a ring and the hole fills in. Any loop on it can slide up to the tip and shrink away — a cone always shrinks to its tip.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A suspension uses two tips, one above and one below. Suspend two points and you get two arcs: a circle.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Suspend the circle and you get a double cone, which is a sphere. Each suspension climbs one dimension.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A wedge glues two spaces together at a single point. Two rings make a figure-eight.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A product: every point of one space paired with every point of the other. A ring times a ring, swept round, is a torus.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Its cells come in pairs: point with point, point with edge, edge with point, edge with edge. That's one point, two edges and one disk.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A quotient collapses part of a space to a single point. Collapse a disk's rim and it closes up into a sphere.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: The rim was a loop, so the shape changed. Collapse something that shrinks to a point and the shape stays the same.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: At each works: click a pedestal to pick up a copy of its space, then click the machine to feed it in.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: New spaces land on the shelf, and you can carry them back in. Lash the Coners. If one plugs a pedestal, click it to pull the plug.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Cone, suspend, wedge, multiply, collapse. Got it.

videos.title: Felling Trees
videos.plays: After the 0-6 intro, before play starts; replayable from the level's “How it works” button
videos.synopsis: Felling trees, slowly: a tree (no cycle) has n − 1 edges and collapses to a point safely; a graph with a cycle — a triangle with a tail — gets a spanning tree marked (n − 1 edges touching every node, the edge that would close the cycle refused), and felling it leaves the unmarked edge as a loop round the surviving hole; collapsing the cycle too kills the hole; χ = nodes − edges and petals = 1 − χ; then the Spool and Cell-Smith controls. Uses both names: nodes (platforms) and edges (walkways).

scenes.title: A tree
scenes.description: A tree of 4 nodes and 3 edges. Gyroid marks each edge amber (n − 1 = 3), then fells it: every node slides into one — a point.

scenes.title: A cycle
scenes.description: A triangle with a tail: 4 nodes, 4 edges. The triangle's three edges glow pink — a cycle — round a dark disk labelled 'hole'.

scenes.title: A spanning tree
scenes.description: Gyroid marks the tail and two sides of the triangle: 3 = n − 1 edges, every node reached. He tries the third side; it flashes red, refused — it would close the cycle.

scenes.title: Fell
scenes.description: The marked tree folds into one node; the unmarked side rounds out into a loop at that node, the hole carried inside it.

scenes.title: The wrong cut
scenes.description: The same graph with all four edges marked violet, cycle included; it collapses to a point and the hole shrinks to nothing.

scenes.title: χ
scenes.description: The petal again; diagram: tree 4 − 3 = 1 → no petals, cycle 4 − 4 = 0 → one petal, petals = 1 − χ.

scenes.title: How to play
scenes.description: Spool marks edges, cycle-closing edges refused; Cell-Smith clicks any node to fell; lash Loop-biters.

scenes.title: Summary
scenes.description: Every connected graph is a bouquet of 1 − χ circles.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A graph is made of nodes — the platforms — joined by edges — the walkways. This one is a tree: it has no cycles.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A tree on $n$ nodes always has exactly $n − 1$ edges. Here: 4 nodes, 3 edges. Gyroid marks them all.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Now he fells it: every edge shrinks, every node slides into one. A tree has no hole in it, so nothing is lost — it’s just a point.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: This graph has a cycle: the triangle. Follow its three edges and you come back where you started.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A cycle goes round a hole. That hole is what makes this space more than a point, and we must not lose it.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: So we don’t fell everything. Gyroid marks a spanning tree: edges that reach every node, never closing a cycle. That takes $n − 1 = 3$ edges.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: The third side of the triangle? Refused. Marking it would close the cycle, and a cycle isn’t a tree.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Every node is touched, no cycle is closed. That’s a spanning tree.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Fell it. The tree shrinks into one node — safe, because a tree has no hole.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: The edge he didn’t mark now starts and ends at that one node: it’s a loop, a petal. The hole is still inside it.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Now the wrong cut: mark every edge, the cycle too, and squash it all.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Everything goes to a point, and the hole dies with it. That’s a different space — Null’s move.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Count nodes minus edges: that’s $χ$. The tree: $4 − 3 = 1$. The cycle graph: $4 − 4 = 0$.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Felling never changes $χ$, and the petals you end with number $1 − χ$.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: On the decks: hold the Spool and click edges to mark a spanning tree. An edge that would close a cycle is refused.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: When the tree reaches every node, take the Cell-Smith and click any node to fell onto it. And lash those Loop-biters.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Mark a tree, keep the cycles. Timber!

captions.text: The cylinder's floor is a space, X. Going up the cylinder is time.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Part of the floor, A, already has a motion chosen for it. Here it's the left point, drifting as time goes up.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: To extend the motion, start with the free point. It only has to start in the right place, so it can just stay put.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Now both ends of the edge are decided. The edge's column simply stretches between them.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A disk is different. Its column has a floor and walls, and the walls are its rim's columns. Until those are decided, it's refused.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: So go in order of dimension: points, then the edges around the disk, then the disk itself.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Why does the disk's column always fill? A box, disk times time, can be squashed onto just its floor and walls.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Shine a light from a point above it: every point of the box lands on the floor or a wall.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: In the Cylinder Works: click a glowing cell on the floor to raise its column.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: If its boundary isn't decided yet, the missing cells flash red.
